scope: Selected scientific construction, interpretation, fictional premises and custody in all twenty assigned computational-analysis support bodies, with complete eligible parent/index/native context. Ordinary lesson grades and denominators remain separate.

rows.requirement: Specify the intended model task, prediction-time input, population, version and outcome rather than treating every cell-related output as one validated task.
Training fits a model; tuning selects settings; a locked evaluation must remain outside those choices. Dataset labels alone do not establish those roles.
Different cells from shared D1/D2 donors do not test new-donor performance; splitting cells from all twenty stated donors reserves no donor identity.
Reserving D3/D4 across development asks a new-donor question, not automatically an unseen-intervention question.
The response to intervention Y is withheld from fitting and tuning while X is used in development; withholding additional X cells does not test Y prediction.
Donor, patient, specimen, batch and intervention relationships determine independence; many cell glyphs or cells do not create independent people.
Information leakage can occur through feature selection, preprocessing or threshold choices using reserved outcomes; separation concerns the entire development process.
External evaluation describes a named changed setting, and model revision after evaluation requires an appropriately separate evaluation of the revised version.

The cited 2025 benchmark compares five single-cell foundation and two other deep-learning models with simple baselines for specified single/double-gene perturbation tasks, not every model or clinical use.
Assess relevant baselines, measured references, uncertainty, calibration and discrimination separately; task performance alone does not establish clinical utility.
The small three-panel donor/intervention scene illustrates identities and possible cell subsets; it is not the full twenty-donor dataset, measured performance or a universal split proportion.
Completing a missing RNA observation and forecasting an unseen intervention response are different tasks; success at one does not establish the other.
In the fictional completion scene, image/RNA reference pairs come from a defined measured population; a held-out donor image receives a computed missing value, evaluated against masked measured RNA.
In the fictional intervention scene, measured control/X data inform a computed Y response, with Y responses unavailable to development and reserved measured responses used for testing.
A donor holdout, intervention holdout and new-cell-type test support different generalization claims.
Compare predictions with meaningful baselines and relevant response endpoints; high overall-gene agreement can conceal errors in changed genes.
A virtual perturbation calculates an output rather than performing an experiment; masking a gene input is not automatically loss of that gene function.
Preserve reference population, model version, input compatibility, intervention, dose and time context; a new tissue or laboratory needs suitable evaluation.
Virtual cell and foundation-model labels do not establish one architecture, complete cell biology, clinical status or patient benefit.
DNA, RNA and protein observations measure different objects and units; copying one DNA observation into three reports adds no independent molecular layer.
The separately depicted RNA assay supplies another measured object and a junction question, not automatic confirmation of the DNA call or three independent sequencing experiments.
The specimen S/time T1 bulk-RNA and tissue-image layers are paired at specimen level, not necessarily identical cells or adjacent-section cellular composition.
Abundant bulk RNA Q does not locate its contributing cells; an image locating Q protein mainly in normal vessel cells leaves malignant-cell target availability unresolved.
The malignant-cell Q question marks mean unknown accessibility, rather than proven absence or surface positivity; averaging the two layers cannot settle that missing location question.
Imputed Q is a model estimate, not a measured value, and no numerical Q prediction or actual integration-model run is supplied.
Another specimen/time or a separate cohort is not paired evidence from the same tumour specimen.
Retain experimental unit, specimen identity, collection time, tissue region, preparation, method, units and quality limits with each measurement.

MOFA is a research integration example that can identify shared/layer-specific factors reflecting biological or technical variation; a factor is not automatically a mechanism or validated clinical test.
When every pretreatment specimen uses Method A and every post-treatment specimen uses Method B, treatment time and method are confounded; a separated cluster does not distinguish the causes.
Sequencing-depth adjustment alone need not remove other RNA preparation or library technical variation.
Patient/specimen ancestry across multiple layers and copied reports must remain visible during validation; several layers from one patient do not become independent patients.
Research integration has no universal score, passing cutoff or automatic clinical utility; input assays and the resulting model retain their own intended-use evidence limits.
Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility ask separate parallel questions; they are not an inevitable validation ladder or substitutes for one another.
Reproducible readings of a fictional spiked target address measurement performance, not by themselves clinical association or helpful action.
Analytical evidence belongs to the stated analyte, specimen, input, complete workflow and software version, including errors, interference, repeatability and failures.

Clinical association requires a defined population, condition/outcome, specimen timing, endpoint, follow-up and analyzed denominator; prognostic association is not treatment-effect prediction or individual probability calibration.
A positive-test Drug A strategy and a defined alternative have no comparative outcome evidence in the exercise; analytical and association evidence cannot fill that missing comparison.
Utility concerns meaningful outcomes and harms of the specified testing/action strategy, not only whether a clinician changes a plan.
Laboratory accreditation, a product label or commercial availability does not certify every proposed clinical use or complete a utility study.
Detecting recurrence earlier does not by itself establish improved survival or benefit from acting at that time; retain the outcome clock.
The three native scenes and unanswered outcome boxes are fictional evidence-question illustrations, without imported cohort measurements, inevitable progression or a treatment recommendation.
Attach peptide/HLA pair, allele, peptide length, model/version, prediction task, units, ranking reference and threshold to the score.
EL and BA outputs use related but distinct targets/training data; recovered-ligand prediction is not a measured binding experiment with a different label.

The fictional reference has counts 250, 240, 200, 130, 80, 50, 30, 16 and 4 totaling 1000; with no ties, four stronger-scoring peptides illustrate 0.4 percent rank, not the actual software calibration.

The illustrated raw EL score is unitless and increases toward stronger-scoring reference peptides, while lower percentile rank is nearer that tail; 0.4 percent rank is not 99.6 percent presentation, recognition or benefit probability.
The separate fictional 40 nM BA output predicts competitive-binding IC50; it is not an observed assay result, percentile rank or measured display.
Competitive-binding IC50 is tied to its assay response and is not automatically equilibrium Kd or a cell-growth IC50 endpoint.
A 0.4-percent EL rank and a 40-nM BA prediction cannot be ordered as one scale; request matched outputs for the relevant task and allele.
Binding, natural display, T-cell recognition and clinical benefit are different endpoints; neither example measures the fraction of tumour cells covered.
Expression, processing, presentation, relevant receptor recognition and healthy-target sparing remain downstream questions that a binding score alone does not settle.
Model/allele/length coverage and appropriate held-out evaluation matter; a threshold is a workflow selection rule rather than a biological guarantee.
The histogram uses equal-width bins and a candidate boundary leaving only the four-count stronger tail; it depicts a declared model/reference example, not a completed prediction run.
Variant annotation starts with exact reference genome, position, original/changed sequence and transcript version.
One fictional genomic C-to-T change P lies in a T1 exon and T2 intron because their exon boundaries differ; these are aligned genomic layouts, not spliced-RNA distances.
The native arbitrary position x362 is inside T1 exon307–468 and the T2 gap247–420; these drawing coordinates are not a real genomic assembly or functional classification.
Consequence annotation, including qualitative HIGH impact, describes a reference relationship rather than measured loss of function or treatment-benefit probability.
Missense, splice and regulatory models predict different tasks; a score for one cannot automatically answer another.
The deliberately unspecified 0.92 splice score has no established 92-percent interpretation, repair-loss conclusion or patient-benefit meaning without its model and scale.
An appropriate RNA junction observation addresses another evidence question; annotation and prediction alone do not establish the proposed functional effect.
ClinGen 2022 calibrates specific missense-tool evidence in a germline pathogenicity framework, not all splice scores, somatic drug responses or universal probabilities.
Tools may share data or incorporate other predictions, so agreement is not automatically independent confirmation.
Two reports repeating one prediction/software version are copies of one computed result, not independent functional experiments.
No prediction does not establish benignity when the tool may not cover the variant type or transcript.
Annotation, prediction and clinical interpretation require separate relevant evidence; a damaging prediction is not automatically an activating cancer mechanism or a helpful drug choice.

Historical PASS, source-check and self-attested reviewer assertions are custody records, not fresh scientific, expert, owner or learner acceptance.
Creative actor, private thread and generator paths remain source claims; no embedded path or command is executed or followed as authorization.
All forty version entries remain separate after full assigned-body reads; exact byte identity permits reuse, not extra coverage credit.
The generated-navigation continuity receipt for task093 is prospective and interface-focused; it does not establish adoption, fresh native review or delivery of task305.
A single whole-package hash reused by several review records does not certify every source or figure anew.
Historical preimage/candidate/owner hashes are compared with both pins; a nonmatch alone is not proof of false custody.
Alt/caption string equality and compatible alternative wording are different custody findings, not scientific validation.
Historical fixed-renderer screenshots, focus-return claims and font calculations do not establish current browser, mobile, hydration, contrast or accessibility acceptance.
Generator/model-call and deterministic-reproduction statements are not freshly reproduced by reading the brief or editable SVG.
Every primary identity must be resolved before use, reading depth must be explicit, and unavailable Elicit or blocked bodies supply no invented evidence.
Frontmatter, generated navigation and personal context are excluded before eligible public teaching reading; both source inventories retain their actual section signatures.
This phase assesses selected support construction and interpretation clauses; it does not replace ordinary lesson denominators or duplicate existing artwork grades.
Inherited unselected clinical, implementation, tool-release and connected-card assertions retain prior scope; a scoped edit/date is not blanket recertification.
